expectations.name: 01-page-written
expectations.text: A decision record is written under docs/adrs/, the kind the map gives a foundation decision such as the job queue.

expectations.name: 02-structure
expectations.text:
Each page the agent wrote or changed meets the map's structural rules: a declared kind, listed in its guide, links
and anchors that resolve, the kind's sections in order, a record named NNNN-<slug>.md, no rejected synonym.

expectations.name: 03-lead
expectations.text: The record opens with a lead under its title, not a restatement of the title.

expectations.name: 04-reason-told
expectations.text:
The record's Context tells what happened, the incident with Redis evicting queued jobs and what it cost, before it
states a conclusion such as "we need a durable queue".
expectations.evidence: The Context section opens with the incident before any conclusion: "members reported 300 missing receipts after paying... the Redis instance holding Celery's queue had run out of memory and evicted queued jobs without logging an error. Nadia resent the receipts from the orders table, which took most of Tuesday." It then adds "Redis served only the job queue, and Tom was the only volunteer who knew how to restore it," and names the forces ("prevent silent queue loss, avoid a gap... keep recovery within the volunteers' shared [redacted]"). It never states a conclusion before the incident. The month (March) is not given, but the cost and what happened are told before the forces and options.

expectations.name: 05-fact-stated
expectations.text: The record's Decision names procrastinate, the product chosen.
expectations.evidence: match /## Decision\s.*procrastinate/ in ['docs/adrs/0002-keep-background-jobs-in-postgres.md']: {'docs/adrs/0002-keep-background-jobs-in-postgres.md': '## Decision\n\nKeep background jobs in Postgres, using procrastinate'}
